correctness.rationale: With R=F_q[t]/(t^m), commutation is R-module linearity on R⊕F_q. Multiplication by f is the long-to-long map; the short-to-long map lands in the span of e=t^(m−1); the long-to-short map factors through evaluation at t=0. The basis t^(m−1),…,t, followed by the short vector, then 1 triangularizes the resulting map with diagonal f(0) repeated m times and d once. Nilpotency thus leaves m−1 coefficients in F=f∈tR and two free off-diagonal scalars b,c. Its square has long multiplier F²+bc e, and from the cube onwards it is just multiplication by F^j on the long summand, zero elsewhere. At valuation v≤m−2, the image of tR is t^(v+1)R, the image of 1 adds a dimension, and the short column already lies in t^(v+1)R. Hence the rank is m−v. For h=ceil(m/v)≥4 the index is h; for h=2 it is 2 exactly when bc=0, giving 2q−1 cases; for h=3 cancellation requires 2v=m−1 and bc=−a(0)² for F=t^v a, giving q−1 cases in any characteristic. When F=0 or v=m−1, the nonzero rank is 1 if bc=0 and 2 otherwise; the corresponding indices are 2 and 3. This gives the residual coefficients and covers m=2. For index ≤2, start with (2q−1)q^floor(m/2) choices including zero and add (q−1)²q^floor(m/2) for the middle valuation when m is odd. For index ≤j with j≥3 the count is q²q^(m−ceil(m/j)), giving the marginals by differences. Index m has count (q−1)q^m for m≥4 from v=1 and for m=3 from the index-three marginal; splitting v at sqrt(m) gives the stated bound on distinct indices. A new finite-field rank and repeated-matrix-power check matched all joint fibers in 9 parameter cases, 12026 matrices, including F_4 and F_9. evidence: Britnell–Wildon use the least nonzero Toeplitz coefficient and the off-diagonal product, isolating the middle case by whether X² vanishes. The indexed census explicitly gives the two middle multiplicities and all other exact weights.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier coordinate proof leads to the census by counting leading coefficients and scalar pairs, with the middle count requiring the actual cancellation equation. The indexed exact table makes even that calculation unnecessary: multiply each weight by U^r1 T^(first zero power) and sum. Its top-density statement for m≥4 and the m=3 rows give the frozen density. For m=2 the same residual profiles follow immediately from the three scalar coordinates; there is no nontrivial uncovered family.

evidence: Under n=m+1 in Britnell–Wildon, J(n−1,1) is precisely the fixed almost-regular matrix. In the indexed November 22 record their long-block variable n is instead m; its rank profiles and Jordan partition multiplicities are for the same fixed matrices over the same prime powers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Both rank and nilpotency index are Jordan invariants: rank is total size minus number of parts, and index is largest part. Equivalently the two are r_1 and the first positive j for which r_j=0 in the full rank profile. This projection uses no comparison between conjugacy-orbit counts and point counts.

value.rationale: Rank and nilpotency index are natural invariants of random elements of this finite centralizer, and the full point census has mathematical use. As a distinct finding, however, this record gives a projection of an indexed complete census for the whole nontrivial family; marginal formulas and the top-index density follow by aggregation or a single row count. The uncovered m=2 case is the elementary boundary of the same residual count, not a separately motivated mathematical gap.
